edges.description: Demodex infestation is associated with recurrent, predominantly external, hordeola; the mechanism linking the mites to the lash-line lesion has not been established.
Obstructed gland orifices precede the staphylococcal infection and abscess formation of the hordeolum.
Staphylococcal growth within a lash-associated eyelid gland drives acute local suppurative inflammation.
Lash-line suppuration produces the external stye centered at the eyelid margin.
The acute suppurative focus at the lid margin is painful.
Local inflammation swells the affected eyelid.
Local inflammation reddens the eyelid around the lesion.
An external hordeolum that does not drain can extend into the eyelid soft tissue as preseptal cellulitis.
An undrained eyelid abscess with preseptal cellulitis can progress to necrosis of the eyelid tissue.
